p: Paul: Paul, against the false accusations of his enemies, displays a clear conscience, for proof of which he repeats the whole course of his life.
And the high priest Ananias commanded: Hypocrites are forced at length to betray themselves by their violence.
Then said Paul unto him: It is lawful for us to complain of injuries, and to summon the wicked to the judgment seat of God, but yet we must do it without hatred, and with a quiet and peaceable mind.
whited wall: This is a vehement and severe speech, but yet not reproachful: for the godly may speak severely, and yet be void of the bitter affection of a severe and angry mind.
contrary to the law: For the Law commands the judge to hear the person that is accused patiently, and to pronounce the sentence judiciously.
Then said Paul: We must willingly and from the heart give honour to magistrates, although they are tyrants.

And when he had so said: The agreement between the wicked is weak, even though they conspire together to oppress the truth.
